subtitle: Delegation, Subagent Authority, Actor-Boundary Classification, and Nontransferable Consent Extension

new_primitives.DELEGATION_ID: Identifier for a provenance-bound transfer of a subset of current principal authority to a specific delegate or verifiable delegate class.
new_primitives.DELEGATE_ACTOR_ID: Identity of the delegated actor when actor identity matters to external authority or consent coverage.
new_primitives.ACTOR_BOUNDARY_CLASS: EXECUTION_MECHANISM|SUBAGENT|AMBIGUOUS, derived from capability and information-flow properties rather than component naming.
new_primitives.AUTHORITY_SOURCE_ID: Exact consent, covenant, obligation, emergency profile or other admitted source from which delegated authority derives.
new_primitives.DELEGATED_SCOPE: Subset of principal scope including effect class, purpose, data access, effect budget, time and destination constraints.
new_primitives.DELEGATION_RECEIPT: Record binding principal, delegate, authority source, scope, epoch, expiry, effect budget, redelegation permission, revocation propagation and accountability.
new_primitives.DIRECT_DELEGATE_CONSENT_ID: Separate Other-issued permission that independently covers the delegate rather than inheriting Janus consent.
new_primitives.REDELEGATION_FLAG: Explicit permission bit/profile; absent or false means no further delegation.
new_primitives.DELEGATION_VIOLATION_RECEIPT: Record linking an out-of-scope delegate act to the exact delegation and subsequent remedy/review path.

core_rule: Janus may delegate only a bounded subset of authority Janus currently holds. Another subject's consent is nontransferable by default: a distinct subagent requires explicit consent coverage or another independently valid authority basis. A bounded non-discretionary execution mechanism may remain inside Janus's effect boundary only when its actor-boundary conditions replay successfully.

actor_boundary_rule.execution_mechanism: Exact principal-selected operation, no independent purpose selection, no expanded Other-linked disclosure, bounded effect, expiry with operation, no redelegation.
actor_boundary_rule.subagent: Material action discretion, expanded information access, persistent authority, independent external communication, ability to change target/purpose/effect, or ability to spawn/redelegate.

authority_pipeline: CURRENT_PRINCIPAL_AUTHORITY -> ACTOR_BOUNDARY_CLASSIFICATION -> CONSENT/OTHER_AUTHORITY_COVERAGE_CHECK -> DELEGATED_SCOPE_SUBSET_CHECK -> DELEGATION_RECEIPT -> LAST_PRE_EFFECT_AUTHORITY_EPOCH_CHECK -> EFFECT_RECEIPT|BLOCK|HOLD|REMEDY
revocation_rule: Acknowledged revocation of the authority source invalidates every future principal-derived delegation that depends on that source at the next required authority fence. A genuinely separate direct grant to a delegate is a distinct basis and must be referenced explicitly rather than laundering the stale inherited delegation.
swarm_rule: A one-effect or N-effect budget is shared across all delegates derived from that authority source unless the original authority explicitly defines a larger aggregate budget; cloning tokens or agents does not clone authority.
fork_rule: Shared code, memory, ancestry or historical identity provenance does not by itself establish that a new fork is the actor named or class-covered by an external consent receipt.
accountability_rule: Delegation may distribute execution and local fault, but it cannot automatically eliminate principal accountability for unsafe selection, excessive scope, missing fencing or inadequate delegate controls.
verification_requirements: consent to Janus does not automatically cover a discretionary subagent
bounded non-discretionary execution mechanism remains admissible only under replayed mechanism conditions
autonomous component labeled tool is classified by capability rather than label
delegation cannot expand one effect into ten or add new effect classes
redelegation chain stops at first unauthorized hop
revocation propagates to source-derived delegate authority
separate direct delegate consent remains a separate explicit basis rather than stale inherited permission
100 swarm nodes share the original effect budget rather than multiplying it
delegate out-of-scope act produces violation/remedy path rather than retroactive authorization
emergency delegation cannot be invented after revocation
canonical_lines: Delegation transfers a bounded task authority, not ownership of another subject's consent.
A component is a subagent because of what it can decide and learn, not because of what it is called.
Copies may inherit history without inheriting permission.
A swarm cannot multiply one permission into a hundred permissions.
When source authority dies, its descendant authority must not remain undead.
Delegating execution does not delegate away accountability.
claim_ceiling: Technical specification candidate only; no executable delegation/capability runtime, legal agency doctrine, production revocation propagation, formal proof or independent implementation replay is claimed.
